correctness.rationale: For fixed exogenous matching, independent uniform priority rankings give h(h−1)/(2n(n−1)) for an extreme advantage per ordered pair; preference is an independent fair coin, proving exact expectation h(h−1)/4. Each school has probability 1/n to host one of t=1,…,h−1 critical candidate sizes, yielding independent school Binomial(t,1/2) clusters except where the same student appears in multiple critical lists. The collision bound ≤(h−1)^4/(2n) and rare-multinomial Poisson convergence give total variation PGF exp[Σ_t(((1+z)/2)^t−1)]. Thus P0→exp(−h+2−2^(−(h−1))) and Var→h(h−1)(h+1)/12. Independent exhaustive permutations for n=2 (16 markets) and n=3 (46656) checked both count definitions and exact mean. Fixed h, n≥h and fixed matching are essential.
